entities.name: Cornelius Haga
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Corneli(u)s Haga was a Dutch ambassador who played a crucial role in establishing diplomatic relations between the Dutch Republic and the Ottoman Empire in the 17th century. He served as the first ambassador of the Dutch Republic to the Ottoman Empire, a position he held from 1638 to 1654.

Haga's mission was to promote trade and commerce between the two nations, and he worked tirelessly to establish favorable trade agreements and strengthen economic ties between the Dutch and Ottoman empires. His efforts were instrumental in securing the Dutch Republic's access to the lucrative spice trade in the Indian Ocean and the Middle East.

The legacy of Cornelius Haga's diplomatic efforts can be seen in the long-lasting impact of Dutch-Ottoman relations on global trade and commerce. His work paved the way for future generations of Dutch diplomats and merchants, who continued to build on the foundations he laid.

'An ambassador is the messenger of the people,' Haga once said, 'and I shall strive to be that messenger for the Dutch people in this great and powerful empire.'
